items.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21
items.q: I don't believe Manuel was dead then. ... Maybe after Nam was dead. Who? Manuel. ... when Manuel had left and went up there to Celestine...

ctx.x: Now you take, you take pretty much all them halls that that time they had, they band. You take the Franz Ami, that was old man Morett in them. Yeah. Old man Morett. Yeah, Morett, yeah. He was a carnet player. That's right. That's right. Old man Morett. You know, you take, you take, of course, you take Manuel, that was his band, the Imperial. Imperial, that's right. You take, they had the economy. Take Freddy Kepler, they were Griffin Church, the Hope Hall they called it at that time. That's right. That's right.
Have you seen the front of that place? It was all blown away? Yes.

items.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21
items.q: That was Nomm in them. ... They had old man George Sims playing biotone. George Davis beating drum. ... You had Buddy Johnson playing trombone.

ctx.x: Just called it that. Just called it that. Because it was that Texas and Pacific railroad, I thought maybe they had a band or something.

No, they meant that band. That was Nomm in them. Nomm, yeah. Nomm. Louis La Rooks? Well, there's Louis La Rooks come after. Nomm. Mineta, that's right. That's right. Yeah. Nomm. Louis La Rooks. Not Nomm. Nomm. Not Louis La Rooks. Louis La Rooks. Louis La Rooks. Louis La Rooks. Joey Hooker? One used to cut meat there. Oh, Louis La Rooks. That's Louis La Rooks. No, they're not. Joel Azard. Oh. Joel Azard. Now, George A Hooker. Then Lodal Rooks come in after. After, after George A Hooker. They had old man George…
